title: עשרת הימים שלא היו
summary: Why 4–15 October 1582 skipped ten days: the tropical year (365.2422 d = 365 d 5 h 49 min), Caesar's leap day every 4 years over-correcting by ~11 min/yr (1 day/128 yr), the spring equinox creeping from 21 March (Nicaea, 325) to 11 March, Lilius/Clavius/Gregory XIII's Inter gravissimas (two parts: delete 10 days + the 4/100/400 rule, 97 leap years per 400, 146,097 days, ~27 s/yr error), Teresa of Ávila, Britain 1752 (11 days), Russia 1918 (13), Orthodox Christmas on 7 January in Jerusalem; the Hebrew calendar's 19-year cycle (235 months, Adar I 7 times; 5787 is a leap year) keeping Passover in spring.
reviewer_verdict: PASS (3 rounds) — nits left: lesson text ~10–15% over the word target (≈25–30 min younger, 30–35 older + challenge); drCv phone axis labels 1582/2026 sit close; old-calendar dashed line unlabelled before 1900
